title: Scales and keys
examples: How do I know if a scale is major or minor?
What is the difference between a tone and a semitone?
Can you show me the pattern for building a scale?

explain.say: Today we will learn about musical scales and keys. A scale is a set of musical notes arranged in order. We use scales to create melodies and harmonies.

draw.text: Scales are ordered sets of notes.

explain.say: A tone is the distance between two notes. It is equal to two semitones. Think of it as a medium-sized step up.
A semitone is the smallest distance between two notes. It is the smallest step you can take in music. Think of it as a very small step.
The major scale has a specific pattern of tones and semitones. The pattern is tone, tone, semitone, tone, tone, tone, semitone. This gives it a bright sound.
The minor scale uses a different pattern of steps. The pattern is tone, semitone, tone, tone, semitone, tone, tone. This gives it a more thoughtful sound.
When you play a song in the key of C major, you are using the C major scale. This means all the notes follow that specific pattern. It is like the song's musical fingerprint.

faq.q: What is the difference between a key and a scale?
faq.a: The scale is the set of notes itself. The key is the tonal center or the overall character of the music built around that scale.
asks: Is the key the same as the scale?
What does it mean to be 'in the key of G?'

faq.q: How do I remember the pattern for major scales?
faq.a: You can remember it as two steps of two, one step of one, and then three steps of two, one step of one. This is the T-T-S-T-T-T-S pattern.
asks: What is the major scale pattern again?
Can you give me a mnemonic for the pattern?

faq.q: Does every scale have to be in the key of C?
faq.a: No, there are many keys. Keys are named after the starting note, like G major or A minor. The starting note sets the whole mood.
asks: Are there keys other than C?
What determines the key of a song?

faq.q: If I change one note, does the whole scale change?
faq.a: Yes, changing one note can change the entire character of the scale. This is how we move from major to minor.
asks: What happens if I raise the third note?

faq.q: Is the minor scale always sad sounding?
faq.a: While minor scales often sound thoughtful or melancholic, they are not always sad. They just have a different emotional quality than major scales.
asks: What emotion does the minor key suggest?

facts: A semitone is the smallest interval distance between two notes.
The major scale pattern is Tone, Tone, Semitone, Tone, Tone, Tone, Semitone.
The minor scale pattern is Tone, Semitone, Tone, Tone, Semitone, Tone, Tone.
The key of a song is determined by its tonic or central note.

quiz.why: This pattern creates the bright, happy sound characteristic of the major key.

wrong.0: Starting with a semitone changes the fundamental feel of the key.
wrong.2: This is too many tones at the start, which is not the standard pattern.
wrong.3: This is actually the pattern for the natural minor scale.

quiz.say: If a scale has the pattern Tone, Semitone, Tone, Tone, Semitone, Tone, Tone, what is it?
quiz.why: This specific sequence of steps defines the natural minor scale structure.

wrong.0: The major scale requires a different, more open pattern of steps.
wrong.1: A chromatic scale uses every single semitone, which is different from this pattern.
wrong.2: While minor is diatonic, this option is too general to identify the specific mood.

quiz.say: Which musical interval is equivalent to two semitones?
quiz.why: By definition, a tone is the distance spanning exactly two semitones.

wrong.0: An octave is a much larger distance, representing eight semitones.
wrong.2: A semitone is only half the distance of a tone.
wrong.3: Whole step is a term used in some systems, but 'Tone' is the standard musical term here.
